claims.text: The local unnumbered-promo catalog models the Pokémon Song Best Collection CD insert group with a January 1, 1999 date.
The local unnumbered-promo group and the local Song Best release both model 11 included card rows.
The local catalogs identify this as a CD insert / CD included reprint promo context rather than a booster release.

The row group assembles card memory through music-media distribution: flagship Pokémon, earlier campaign reprints, glossy trainer variants, and an English Base Set Pikachu caveat all meet inside one CD object.
The richer local Song Best rows credit Mitsuhiro Arita, Ken Sugimori, Christopher Rush, Hiromichi Sugiyama, Sumiyoshi Kizuki, and Keiji Kinebuchi across the 11-card witness set.

Because Song Best rows are unnumbered promo/campaign rows, an agent must identify the card by name, Song Best CD insert route, variant notes, language caveats, and source-index context rather than by printed set number alone.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent result says Pokémon Song Best Collection, Song Best CD, CD insert, unnumbered Song Best promo, or one of the 11 Song Best card names.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Confirm the Song Best CD insert route and row-specific caveats before treating a card as this unnumbered promo group.
steps: Confirm the claimed card is one of the 11 modeled Song Best rows.
Preserve the Song Best Collection CD insert / reprint context separately from the card name.
Check row-specific caveats: earlier campaign reuse, glossy trainer variant, Computer Error print lane, or English Pikachu inclusion.
Do not merge with No Rarity, Toyota, World Hobby Fair, Nintendo 64, CoroCoro, Kamex, or ordinary Base/Fossil-style rows without the matching route evidence.
For transactional use, ask for front, back, surface, stock/gloss, language, and any CD/booklet/packaging provenance photos.
not_claiming: official product-boundary proof beyond cited catalogs

narrative.human_title: When the cards arrived inside the music
narrative.why_it_matters: Song Best is beautiful because it does not behave like a set. It feels like Pokémon assembling itself sideways: songs, booklets, campaign leftovers, classic monsters, a glossy Computer Error lane, even an English Pikachu sitting inside a Japanese product story. The CD turns cards into liner notes for the franchise. For an agent, that means the route is not decorative; it is the identity.

narrative.human_title: The mascot as the language caveat
narrative.why_it_matters: Song Best Pikachu is a perfect trap for lazy cataloging. It is Pikachu, yes, but the interesting part is that the richer row marks it as an English Base Set card inside a Japanese CD product. The mascot is almost too familiar; the language boundary is where the real story lives.
